speaker: SPEAKER_01
text: Mr. President, I ask consent that my chief of staff, John Donenberg, be allowed to join me on the floor here.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Without objection.

speaker: SPEAKER_01
text: Thank
you, Mr. President.

speaker: SPEAKER_04
text: Mr.

speaker: SPEAKER_01
text: President, I rise today to recognize an extraordinary public servant who is leaving my office for a

speaker: SPEAKER_08
text: new role.

speaker: SPEAKER_08
text: John Donnenberg has been one of my most trusted senior advisors since 2011 when I first ran for the United States Senate.

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: After his stint advising me on policy during the 2012 campaign, I asked John to serve as my first legislative director in my Senate office. John was my LD for six years, then senior advisor and policy director for Warren for President. And for the last four years, he has served as my Chief
of State.

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: After nearly a dozen years of working together, I have come to know John pretty well, so I can say with some authority that he is one of the best policy nerds and sharpest minds on economic policy in the business.

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: When I arrived in the Senate, I knew more than pretty much anybody else in the world about a very specific slice of commercial law. I also had spent a lot of time thinking about how middle class families were getting crushed by an economy that didn't work for them and thinking through how to fix it. And this was a good start, but being a senator means doing work on a much, much broader range of issues.

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: John was the person I turned to for counsel as I developed that broader agenda, drawing on his deep expertise with policy, his facility for digging into data, and his formidable technical training. Also, importantly, John has good values.
The

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: long-standing belief that government is here to serve not the richest and most powerful, not those who can hire armies of lobbyists and lawyers, but here to serve the people who are trying to build a future for themselves and their families. John and I were a good match, and I will say that, when I'm not saying, as part of that, that we always saw our next moves the same way.
But he

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: has a lightning quick mind, a staggering command of both domestic and foreign policy topics and instincts honed by years of working in Congress. And those qualities allowed him to see around corners I didn't even know existed. He's good with numbers and he's never been afraid

speaker: SPEAKER_10
text: to change his mind based on what the data show him. Our relationship has always been energetic.
John

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: hasn't been afraid to tangle with me when he thought I was getting something wrong. He would tell me I was making a mistake and I would tell him he didn't know what he was talking about. We would size each other up and I would start lobbing fastballs at him just like I was back in the classroom trying to figure out if a student had done the reading and was on solid ground in their arguments. John of course has always, always done the reading.

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: He would grab those fastballs out of the air and zing them back at me with a spin, often highlighting an aspect to the issue I had failed to consider. Sometimes I would try a
new

speaker: SPEAKER_11
text: angle, play the devil's advocate to see if he could defend his position, back and forth until I had, often in the space of

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: 10 or 15 minutes, pressure tested an argument more thoroughly than seemed possible. Now, I'm not saying John won all those arguments.

speaker: SPEAKER_12
text: But I give him a 50/50 lifetime record, which is pretty respectable in my book. And I'd also say
this:

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: 100% of the time, my thinking about an issue got deeper and sharper as a result of running my views through the gauntlet of John's scrutiny.
Given

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: all these attributes, it should come as no surprise that John had a very specialized skill that is rarely employed among adults

speaker: SPEAKER_11
text: outside elected office. John was a whiz at debate prep. He has worked with me and several other senators during our races, helping candidates prepare for pre-election debates.

speaker: SPEAKER_11
text: He put all of us through our paces, forcing us to confront the frustration and the

speaker: SPEAKER_16
text: opportunities of butting heads with our opponents and doing it in one-minute chunks. For all of us who

speaker: SPEAKER_17
text: managed to survive those debates far better than we expected, we owe John our thanks.
When he

speaker: SPEAKER_08
text: came to work for me, John brought with him years of experience in Congress. Before joining my office, John served as Chief

speaker: SPEAKER_20
text: Counsel to Senator Richard Blumenthal. Before then, he served as Health Law Advisor to

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: Representative Henry Waxman on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and the House Energy and Commerce Committee. I asked Henry Waxman for a few words about John, and he had this to say:
John

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: started his congressional career

speaker: SPEAKER_20
text: as a precocious young staffer in my office working on the Affordable Care Act. He's leaving Senator Warren's staff
as a

speaker: SPEAKER_20
text: veteran chief of staff with many distinguished legislative accomplishments. What's been constant is

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: the gratitude and respect he has earned from everyone who has been lucky enough to work with him along the
way.
John's

speaker: SPEAKER_09
text: first

speaker: SPEAKER_08
text: experience working in Congress has a special resonance for me. John was a legal fellow for Senator Ted Kennedy, the senior senator from Massachusetts who served for 47 years in the seat I
now hold.

speaker: SPEAKER_21
text: I think Senator Kennedy would be pleased to know that the young man he first brought in for work in the federal legislature ended up contributing so much to this work.
There is

speaker: SPEAKER_13
text: one more aspect of John's leadership that I want to make sure to highlight. He is a dedicated mentor

speaker: SPEAKER_21
text: who has trained scores of policy staffers in how to make this country work better for families who don't always have someone in government looking out for
them.

speaker: SPEAKER_21
text: Year after year, I have observed as John invests in the staff on my team and throughout government, supporting them,

speaker: SPEAKER_24
text: teaching them, and challenging them, and always, always, always making them better at what they do. Congress is a hard place to work in a lot of ways.

speaker: SPEAKER_24
text: John often tells me that trying to make change by working in the Senate can feel a lot like running face-first into a brick wall over and over and over again. You have to

speaker: SPEAKER_20
text: keep standing up and sprinting back at the wall because even though history suggests you're

speaker: SPEAKER_13
text: going to smack right into it just like last time, the only way you'll ever smash through the bricks is by taking one more run at it.
John is

speaker: SPEAKER_21
text: the kind of colleague who makes you want to take one more run

speaker: SPEAKER_20
text: at knocking down the wall that has never been knocked down before. The one who will help you dust yourself off and then sprint along beside you.
I've watched as

speaker: SPEAKER_11
text: these staffers who John has trained have transformed from eager, gifted beginners into seasoned strategists. John and I have stood proudly side by side

speaker: SPEAKER_11
text: as we've seen them leave our office and take their talents to go make change somewhere else. John's commitment to mentorship means that today we have more dedicated public servants

speaker: SPEAKER_13
text: doing top-notch work all around the country and doing it better because of their time learning from
him.

speaker: SPEAKER_11
text: Now John is the one who is taking his talents to another public service post.

speaker: SPEAKER_11
text: He is headed to the White House to serve as deputy director of the National Economic Council. I know John will bring with him to this position an abiding commitment to helping working families, as well

speaker: SPEAKER_29
text: as one of

speaker: SPEAKER_08
text: the best policy brains in the business.
One last note. John is a

speaker: SPEAKER_08
text: good man. He is honest. He is principled. He is generous. He is funny. He cares about people.
He

speaker: SPEAKER_08
text: loves his family deeply, and he is always there for

speaker: SPEAKER_11
text: his friends. He tries

speaker: SPEAKER_24
text: to live his life every day according to deeply held moral values. I admire
him.

text: So, John, I am grateful down to my toes for the years that we have worked

speaker: SPEAKER_11

Thank you
